To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a peptide-based, fully artificial diagnostic reagent that is significantly better than tuberculins for identifying skin test negative cattle infected with M. bovis and that this reagent is not compromised by BCG vaccination.

we have developed a novel peptide cocktail for the detection of M. bovis in cattle that outperforms the tuberculin skin test, does not cross-react with M. bovis BCG, and is amenable to large-scale production.

a peptide cocktail, consisting of peptides derived from four immunodominant antigens, was superior to tuberculin for detecting M. bovis infection in cattle and did not cross-react with BCG-vaccinated cattle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new diagnostic tool for the identification of cattle infected with M. bovis and the discrimination of vaccinated animals.
the identification of novel antigens that can be used to develop improved diagnostic tools with which to identify cattle infected with M. bovis.

the development of improved immunodiagnostic reagent for bovine tuberculosis, a disease that is a serious threat to cattle and wildlife worldwide and that is responsible for substantial economic and social costs.
